findings.quote: Ask a native Ukrainian teacher or tutor to write one known word in their own hand.
findings.explanation: Lesson 2 promises print-to-handwriting recognition but supplies printed words and verbal clues. The learner cannot practise the promised visual distinction using the supplied lesson alone; the final summary nevertheless claims this skill.

In act-wb-fill, the keyed answer нь duplicates the existing final ь; the offered н fits the displayed blank. The same mismatch occurs in «Золота о́сі__ь настала.» with answer нь. This teaches incorrect completion and can penalize correct reasoning. VESUM verification was attempted but blocked, so dictionary confirmation remains unresolved.

findings.quote: Розбийте слово на відкриті та закриті частини:
findings.explanation: The lesson never defines open versus closed syllables or models their contrast before asking learners to identify three open syllables. Counting vowels alone does not teach this distinction. This untranslated instruction also sits in an extended Ukrainian explanation without aligned English support, making the new task harder to understand at early A1.

findings.quote: Українське о залишається чистим; читай молоко́ у три відкриті удари.
findings.explanation: Lesson 2, act-4: «у три відкриті удари» is unnatural reading metalanguage, apparently transferred from English syllable beats. It obscures the intended instruction to read three open syllables. Dictionary verification was attempted but blocked; this finding rests on editorial linguistic judgment.

Lesson 3, act-l3-wb-fill: «головна столиця» is an unnecessarily inflated collocation in this context. The adjective suggests multiple capitals ranked by importance, whereas the sentence simply identifies Ukraine's capital. Dictionary verification was attempted but blocked.

findings.quote: Олена: Молодець, читаєш дуже чисто й плавно!
findings.explanation: Across the three lessons, the same characters primarily quiz and praise one another. The final dialogue repeats this classroom performance instead of giving the learner a compelling reason to read or discover something. Named characters alone do not make the exchanges feel human.

findings.quote: У слові «молоко» всі три звуки [о] звучать чітко.
findings.explanation: This Lesson 2 inline statement repeats the immediately preceding matching and quiz checks of молоко. The same feature returns in act-reading-check and workbook practice. Similar recycling dominates Lesson 3. Although repetition is explicitly justified, changing activity formats seldom adds discrimination, transfer, or an engaging reading purpose.

findings.quote: Під час читання довших слів не поспішайте й не називайте окремі літери:
findings.explanation: Lesson 3 switches to sustained Ukrainian instructional metalanguage without the accessible English support that establishes the teacher's voice in Lessons 1–2. The resulting formal lecture register is a substantive A1 single-voice failure, independent of immersion percentages.

findings.quote: Вітаємо з успішним завершенням модуля! — Congratulations on successfully completing the module!
findings.explanation: The closing voice becomes ceremonial and congratulatory, assuming demonstrated success merely from reaching the summary. Together with repeated evaluative praise in the dialogues, this weakens the otherwise restrained adult-peer tone.
